The five teaching chapters are LESSON["lecture"]'s five parts, in its order and in its words; the pictures are the lesson's own drawings (the zoom, the globe and its catch, the dig, the sky, the sun-and-shade cups). Only the four content objectives are claimed: the film shows the globe catch and the cup test, but it does not teach predicting or recording, so no TWS or SIC code is listed.
title: Our Earth, Our Sun
subtitle: Grade 1 Science
objectives: Know that Earth is the planet on which we live.
Know that Earth is mostly covered in water.
Describe land as being made of rock and soil.
Describe the Sun as a source of heat and light, and as one of many stars.

beats.say: This is our Earth, and this is our Sun.
What is Earth made of? And what does the Sun give us?
Start at your house. Now zoom out, and there is your town.
Zoom out again, and there is your whole country.
Zoom out once more. There is the whole Earth, a round planet floating in space.
Earth is the planet we live on. Everyone you know lives on it.
The ground looks flat, because Earth is so big. From space, it is round.
Look at Earth from space. Most of it is blue.
Blue is water. That is the sea. Green is land.
Is there more water, or more land? Catch a globe ten times to find out.
Each time, look under your finger. Is it on blue water, or on green land?
Seven catches landed on water, and three on land.
There is more water than land. Earth is mostly water.
What is land made of? Dig down through the grass.
First there is soil, dark and crumbly. Plants grow in it.
In the soil are small stones. A stone is a tiny piece of rock.
Dig deeper. The soil runs out, and you hit hard rock.
So land is soil on top, and rock underneath, everywhere.
A pebble is a small piece of rock. A mountain is a huge piece of rock.

scenes.heading: The Sun gives light and heat

beats.say: At night there is no Sun. It is dark, and it is cooler.
The Sun rises, and light fills the sky.
At midday the Sun is high. It warms the ground, the sea and your skin.
Put one cup of water in the sun. Put one in the shade.
Wait an hour. The cup in the sun gets warmer. The shade one stays cool.
The Sun is a source of light and heat. Both come from the Sun.

at.source: a source of light and heat

beats.say: Never look straight at the Sun. It is so bright it can hurt your eyes.
At night the sky is full of tiny lights. They are stars.
Each star is a huge ball of hot, glowing gas, very far away.
The Sun is a star too. It looks big because it is the nearest one.
Earth is our planet. The Sun is our star.
Earth is the planet we live on. Most of it is water.
Land is soil on top, and rock underneath.
The Sun gives us light and heat. It is our nearest star.
Now you know your Earth and your Sun.
